author: Tieleneez
quote: Ocarina of Time captured something that modern gaming has largely lost: the genuine sense of discovery. Back then, you couldn't simply look everything up online. You had to explore, experiment, get lost, solve puzzles and stumble upon secrets yourself. Every hidden cave, mysterious character and unexplored corner felt like an invitation to adventure. It wasn't just about completing a game; it was about discovering a world. That sense of wonder is what made Ocarina of Time so special, and why it remains so memorable to this day.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998)

author: Tieleneez
quote:
Grand Theft Auto was historically built around an exaggerated but recognizable portrayal of American society. Its criminal underworld, gang hierarchies, institutional corruption and social dysfunction drew inspiration from actual human behaviour and social structures. GTA was vulgar, cynical and irreverent, but its satire had a foundation in recognizable reality.

GTA VI seems to represent a departure from that philosophy.

My criticism of Lucia as a central criminal protagonist isn't simply that she's a woman. It's that the criminal world GTA draws inspiration from is overwhelmingly male-dominated, particularly at the highest levels of organized crime. This isn't merely a cultural stereotype; criminological research documents substantial gender disparities in criminal networks, authority and access to leadership positions.

Women certainly participate in organized crime, and some become influential leaders. But exceptions shouldn't be confused with the general structure of a social phenomenon. Fictional representation should account for these realities rather than treat demographic representation as an independent creative objective.

The same concern extends to Rockstar's approach to satire. A franchise once characterized by indiscriminate irreverence now appears increasingly conscious of contemporary cultural sensitivities. It still has violence, profanity, nudity and vulgarity, but being explicit isn't the same as being genuinely transgressive. Its jokes about contemporary culture can feel recycled, while its willingness to challenge prevailing sensibilities appears more selective.

This is the contradiction: Rockstar seems interested in preserving the aesthetics of rebellion without necessarily preserving the creative philosophy that made the franchise rebellious.

The issue isn't diversity, female characters or emotional storytelling in themselves. It's the possibility that ideological considerations are increasingly taking precedence over anthropological realism, sociological correspondence and artistic consistency.

GTA VI might still look dangerous, sound vulgar and behave like Grand Theft Auto. But if its creative priorities have shifted from interpreting reality to accommodating contemporary ideological expectations, then what remains is increasingly the aesthetic of transgression rather than transgression itself.

author: Tieleneez
quote: A remarkable remake of an all-time classic. Nintendo has managed to modernise Ocarina of Time without compromising its original identity. The visual overhaul is impressive, bringing Hyrule to life with incredible environmental detail, improved character models, lighting and animations. Combined with the reworked orchestral soundtrack and improved sound design, the atmosphere feels more immersive than **** gameplay also benefits from modern controls, full camera movement and several quality-of-life improvements. Importantly, the original dungeon design, puzzles and progression remain largely intact. This is still the Ocarina of Time people fell in love with, just brought up to modern **** only criticism is that Nintendo could have been more ambitious with additional content, particularly the absence of Master Quest. Nevertheless, this is a carefully executed remake that respects its source material rather than unnecessarily reinventing it.A timeless classic, properly brought into the modern era.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Tieleneez
quote:
Phantom Blade Zero – Flashy, challenging and incredibly fun

I'm having a lot of fun with Phantom Blade Zero. It's one of those games that keeps you wanting to try again, especially when you're fighting bosses. And believe me, some of those fights can be quite challenging!What I particularly enjoy is the combat. It's flashy, stylish and spectacular to look at, but there's also a surprising amount of deliberation behind it. You can't just keep attacking and expect to get away with it. You have to pay attention, wait for the right moment, parry, parry again, and then find your opening to unleash your own attacks. It's almost like a dance between you and your opponent. Defend, read your enemy, find the opening and strike. When everything comes together, it feels incredibly **** game definitely has some Soulslike elements, particularly when it comes to its challenging bosses and the importance of timing. However, I wouldn't necessarily call it a Soulslike. Its combat has a different rhythm and personality. It feels much more like a cinematic martial arts action game, where the fights are built around spectacular combinations and well-timed defensive **** that's probably what I enjoy most about it. The combat makes you feel powerful, but it also reminds you that you still have to earn your victories. Boss fights can be frustrating at times, but overcoming them is genuinely **** the end of the day, I don't need a game to be perfect to enjoy it. I want engaging gameplay, challenging encounters and, most importantly, to have fun. Phantom Blade Zero delivers on those fronts for ****'s stylish, challenging, satisfying and, above all, a lot of fun to play.
